2. The fact of the case that petitioner as pre-emptor filed pre-emption case No.159 of 2007 before the Court of Learned Assistant Judge, Pirgacha, Rangpur against the purchaser-pre-emptee and others under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption of the suit land described in the schedule of the petition and kabla No. 2970 dated 30-7-2007, sale deed No. 3082 dated 30-8-2007 and 3340 dated 19-8-2007 registered in the office of the Sub-registrar, Pirgacha, Rangpur. The pre-emptee-purchaser entered appearance in the case and was contesting the case by filing written objection and on 30-7-2008 the case was posted for peremptory hearing. On 30-7-2008 the pre-emptor filed an application under section 96(3)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 to calculate the interest upon the deed value which was heard and allowed by learned Assistant Judge, Pirgacha Court, Rangpur on 24-9-2008 and the learned Judge of the trial court directed the serestadar to calculate the interest and to submit the report. Accordingly the serestadar calculated the interest which stands Taka 1,021.37 and submitted his report on 13-10-2008 and after accepting the report the learned trial court ordered the pre-emptor to deposit the interest by chalan and accordingly the pre-emptor on 22-10-2008 deposited the interest by chalan and submitted that chalan to the court and the learned Judge of the trail court ordered to keep the chalan with the record. 

 5. Mr Sadananda Rana along with Mr Md Shibbir Ahmed learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Advocate for the pre-emptor did not advise her to deposit the interest along with the application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as such she could not deposited the interest amount along with the application though the other two conditions as per provision of sections 96(3) of the Act, 1950 have been fulfilled. Such failure to deposit the interest money is attributed to the latches and negligence of the learned advocate for which the client could not be penalized. In this context he referred the case of Kabir Ahmed Sawdagar vs Md Syed Saifuddin Jaheed and others reported in 58 DLR 277. Learned Advocate further submits that the deposit of the interest in the court at the time of the filing the case though mandatory yet due to bonafide mistake the learned lawyer could not advise his client to deposit the interest amount as per the new amendment as such the order passed by the learned District Judge, is not sustainable. In support of this submission Mr Ahmed referred two decisions reported in 42 DLR (AD) 77 and 52 DLR 289. 

 7. I have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner, perused the Rule, record and other connected papers kept in the judicial file. It appears that admittedly the deed in question was executed and registered on 30-7-2007, 6-8-2007 and 19-8-2007 and the application for pre-emption was filed on 24-9-2007. It is note-worthy to mention here that the application for pre-emption has been filed under the amended provision of section 96 of State Acquisition & Tenancy Act, 1950. The said amendment has been introduced by substituting the former section 96 by Act No. XXXIV of 2006. Accordingly, at the time of filing the application for pre-emption the pre-emptor as per requirement of new section 96(3)(a) & (b) deposited the amount of the consideration money mentioned in the deed of sale as well as compensation at the rate of 25% of the amount of mentioned in the deed of sale. But did not deposit 8% simple interest on the sale deed from the date of execution of the deed to the filing of the application of the pre-emption as provided in clause (c) Sub-section 3 of section-96. Subsequently the pre-emptor filed an application for calculation of interest and upon such calculation by the office (Seresta) of the learned court the pre-emptor deposited the said amount on 22-10-2008.
